stemBlocks.value: A cliff AB is 36 m high, with B at sea level. From the top A, the angle of depression of a boat at C is 28°. a) Explain why the angle of elevation of A from C is also 28°. b) Calculate the horizontal distance BC. c) The boat moves 25 m directly towards B. Calculate the new angle of elevation of A, to the nearest degree.
Think first: The horizontal at the cliff top and the sea surface are parallel, so the depression and elevation angles are alternate angles.

stemBlocks.altText: Source visual for edmar-csec-p176-q02 from workbook page 176.

contentBlocks.value: The horizontal line at A and the sea-level line through B and C are parallel, and AC is a transversal
Result: depression at A and elevation at C are alternate angles

solutionSteps.instruction: State the conclusion for part a.

contentBlocks.value: Alternate angles between parallel lines are equal
Result: angle of elevation of A from C = 28°

solutionSteps.instruction: Use the tangent ratio in triangle ABC.
Compute the new angle with inverse tangent.

strategyBlocks.value: Justify the equal angles from parallel horizontals, use tan 28° to get BC, subtract 25 m and use the inverse tangent for the new angle.

finalAnswerBlocks.value: (a) The horizontal at A is parallel to sea level, so the angle of depression at A and the angle of elevation at C are alternate angles between parallel lines and are therefore equal, both 28°  (b) BC ≈ 67.7 m  (c) the new angle of elevation is approximately 40°

whyThisWorks.value: Angles of depression and elevation are always measured from a horizontal, and all horizontals in a vertical plane are parallel — so the alternate-angle rule makes the two angles equal every time. As the boat comes closer the same 36 m height is seen across a shorter base, so the tangent ratio grows and the angle of elevation increases, which is exactly what the calculation confirms.
